name: protocol-to-tlfs
title: Protocol to TLFs
description: Take a study from its protocol (or its USDM study definition) and SDTM to validated ADaM, ARD and rendered TLFs by running the team-owned sub-workflows in order, each as its own run with its own reviewers: digitize-protocol when the package has a protocol but no USDM (clinical scientist + standards reviewer) -> plan-tlfs (statistician) -> validate-with-core of the SDTM (standards reviewer) -> specify-analyses (statistician) -> derive-and-validate-adam: derive-adam gated by CORE ADaMIG validation (ADaM programmer + standards reviewer) -> generate-ard-tlfs (statistical programmer + statistician) -> trace-deliverables (no AI: one traceability explorer page linking every number back to SDTM and every output back to the protocol); when the TLF review finds the analysis itself wrong, its request goes back to specify-analyses and the ADaM and TLFs are regenerated (at most two rounds). The sub-workflows hand each other a study package of files by download URL; nothing is copied by hand. The AI writes plans, specs and code; scripts execute the code, validate, and produce every number; humans approve at every hand-off. Each sub-workflow also runs on its own, so a sponsor can adopt any one of them.
preamble: CDISC terms (USDM, SDTM, ADaM, ARS, ARD, TLF, CORE rule IDs, Define-XML, adverse events, deaths) are technical workflow content.

triggerInput.name: package
triggerInput.description: Optional study package { study, profile, files: [{ name, downloadUrl, kind, sha256 }] } with kinds usdm or protocol (a protocol without a USDM is digitized first), sdtm (+ sdtm-define, sap). Leave empty: the statistician uploads the USDM, SDTM and define.xml in the planning run.

steps.name: Route the input
steps.description: Deterministic. A package with a USDM goes straight to planning; a package with a protocol but no USDM is digitized first (and comes back here with the USDM); an empty package goes to planning, where the statistician uploads the inputs.

steps.name: Digitize the protocol
steps.description: Child run of digitize-protocol: the AI turns the protocol PDF into a USDM 4.0 study definition with a page citation for every entity; a gate checks the schema, references and quotes; CDISC CORE validates it; the clinical scientist approves.

steps.name: Plan the TLFs
steps.description: Child run of plan-tlfs: a deterministic data check first compares the SDTM with the USDM (arms, enrollment, exposure; a mismatch stops the run at data-mismatch); the AI plans every output from the USDM and checks feasibility against the SDTM; a gate checks every trace; an independent AI critic audits it; the statistician approves. Uploads happen here when no package was given.

steps.name: Validate with CDISC CORE (SDTM)
steps.description: Child run of validate-with-core against SDTMIG: the standards reviewer records a disposition per finding; a 'fix' asks for corrected SDTM inside that run.

steps.name: Route to specification
steps.description: Deterministic. Hands specify-analyses the validated package; when the TLF review asks for a spec change, sends the package back with the reviewer's request (at most two rounds, then a human takes over).

steps.name: Specify the analyses
steps.description: Child run of specify-analyses: ARS-aligned analysis specs, the ADaM spec and an ARS ReportingEvent, gated against the ARS schema and every cross-reference; the statistician approves.

steps.name: Derive and validate ADaM
steps.description: Child run of derive-and-validate-adam: derive-adam (the AI writes traced programs, scripts run them) gated by CORE ADaMIG validation, looping on findings marked 'fix' (at most three derivation rounds).

steps.name: Generate ARD and TLFs
steps.description: Child run of generate-ard-tlfs: the AI writes one program per output, scripts run them and reconcile every displayed number with the ARD; the reviewer approves in the TLF viewer.

steps.name: Trace the deliverables
steps.description: Child run of trace-deliverables (deterministic, no AI): one traceability explorer page linking every TLF number to its ARD rows, ARS analysis, ADaM variables, derivation code and SDTM columns; every output to its protocol objective, endpoint and page; every CORE finding to the variables and outputs it touches; and the checks per output. Not a gate: if it fails, the run still delivers generate-ard-tlfs's package and the TLF viewer, and says so.

steps.name: Collect the deliverables to show
steps.description: Deterministic. Hands the files worth opening (traceability explorer - or the TLF viewer when trace-deliverables did not finish - reconciliation, USDM / plan / spec review pages, CORE reports per standard, ADaM define.xml) out of the final study package on as downloaded files, so finish can show them in this run.

steps.name: Assemble the deliverables
steps.description: Deterministic. Shows the deliverables in this run - the traceability explorer (displays, ARD, programs, ADaM lineage, protocol, CORE and checks in one page), reconciliation, the USDM, plan and spec review pages, the CORE reports and the ADaM define.xml, each sha256-verified - and lists every file of every sub-workflow with the run that produced it in manifest.json.

steps.name: TLF review still asks for a spec change after two rounds
The SDTM is not the protocol's study, or cannot answer a primary objective
A sub-workflow ended without a result
